title: Ordered tool-call segments dropped after proxy retry leading to partial structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported that multi-part tool/function call responses occasionally arrive with missing trailing fields in the structured output (JSON blobs truncated or keys missing). This manifests as parse errors in customer code and incorrect downstream tool invocations. Reports span Hosted and Dedicated tiers and one Private on-prem deployment that uses our proxy layer. Issue appears under high concurrency with bursts and correlates with proxy retry events.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use the sample harness (loadgen-toolcall) to send 200 concurrent requests that trigger multi-toolcall streaming responses (two tool payloads + final metadata JSON).
2) Configure upstream proxy retries to 2 and enable HTTP/2 multiplexing (default behavior in our front proxy).
3) Observe ~0.5-2% of responses where final metadata JSON is missing closing braces or trailing keys (e.g., "debug": {...} omitted).
4) Reproduce more reliably by inserting artificial network jitter between the second tool payload and the final metadata chunk to force a retry.
investigation_notes: - Customer ticket IDs: CUST-40412 (Hosted), CUST-40501 (Dedicated), CUST-40589 (Private).
- Logs show proxy retry timestamps align with responses missing final metadata chunks.

- Our stream reassembly component assigns an incremental segment sequence for each connection, but when upstream proxy retries the backend TCP request we observed reuse of the same sequence IDs, causing the reassembly map to overwrite earlier segments.
- KV cache miss pattern increases likelihood because longer back-and-forth increases window for a proxy retry to be triggered.
- Parser unit tests did not cover cross-retry reassembly ordering; integration harness did not simulate proxy-driven retry duplication.
- Private customer's on-prem proxy had an older configuration with aggressive retry/backoff; that helped reproduce quickly.
- No evidence of model runtime truncation; the full payload reaches the first backend attempt in most traces. The loss occurs during the retry-and-merge path.
root_cause: The proxy retry path can replay partial HTTP chunk streams with duplicate segment IDs. The stream reassembly layer uses per-connection monotonically-incrementing IDs but reuses the same ID space when the proxy opens a new backend connection for a retried request, causing later segments to overwrite earlier ones in the reassembly buffer. The parser expects strictly ordered, non-duplicated segments and therefore consumes a truncated/incomplete JSON when final metadata is overwritten.
fix_plan: 1) Short-term mitigation: add a proxy-config toggle to disable application-level retries for /v1/toolcall and /v1/functions endpoints and notify affected customers. (Done for Hosted; applied to Dedicated clusters on 2026-03-12).

2) Immediate patch: change stream reassembly to namespace sequence IDs by (connection_id, attempt_id) instead of a flat sequence so replays cannot overwrite in-flight segments. Implement sequence deduplication and holdback window to reorder by explicit sequence numbers emitted by runtime. (PR linked below).

3) Parser hardening: make the structured-output parser tolerant of split tokens across segment boundaries by buffering until a valid JSON object close is observed and validating trailing delimiter markers.
4) Add server-side assertion that final metadata chunk contains expected magic footer token; if missing, request backend to resend the missing chunk (idempotent fetch).
5) Add telemetry and histogram for retry-reassembly collisions to monitor post-rollout.
6) Postmortem and customer-facing RCA after stable rollout.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for reassembly namespacing and deduplication (new tests added to runtime/streaming/tests).
- Integration test that simulates proxy retry by closing backend connection mid-stream and replaying remainder on a new connection, asserting complete reconstruction.
- Fuzz tests for split-token structured JSON across chunks.
- Canary e2e test against a 10% traffic slice with synthetic customers that exercise toolcall+parser flows.
- Load test at 2x peak concurrency for 30 minutes to validate behavior under bursty KV-miss patterns.
- Manual validation with previously-impacted customers' sample workloads (coordinated test windows).
rollout_plan: - 2026-03-14: Merge PR into canary branch and deploy to canary region A (10% of Hosted control plane traffic).
- 2026-03-15: Monitor retry-collision metric and parser error rate for 48 hours. If stable, roll to remaining Hosted regions and Dedicated clusters with staged gates (20% -> 50% -> 100%).
- 2026-03-17: For Private customers, provide patch bundle and guidance; offer remote assist for on-prem proxy config changes.
- Rollback plan: revert stream reassembly change and re-enable proxy retries if unknown regression appears; fallback will re-enable the proxy-toggle applied in step (1) while investigating.
- Communication: enable status updates on the customer incident portal after each rollout gate.
customer_notifications: 2026-03-11: Initial acknowledgement sent to affected customers with temporary mitigation steps and request for workload samples.
2026-03-13: Notified Dedicated customers that proxy retries were disabled for toolcall endpoints as a mitigation; offered immediate rollback if they require default retry behavior.
2026-03-14: Will share post-fix ETA and schedule coordinated verification windows.
follow_up_tasks: - ENG-99902: Add structured-output chunk footer token to protocol and update runtime to emit it.
- ENG-99905: Extend observability to correlate parsing failures to specific proxy configurations.
- PM-421: Draft customer-facing RCA and update docs on recommended proxy settings for on-prem deployments.
- DES-212: Update error-state messaging in Console to show parsing-retry collisions and mitigation steps.
